A user hive file is opened by turning on the backup and restore privileges and mounting it under a temporary name in the machine registry. When the mount succeeds, the source is writable: edits go straight into the mounted hive and take effect when the source is closed. When it yields no key, the hive opens as an empty scratch policy store the person can edit, but nothing is written back to the hive file. (PolicyPlus/PolicyLoader.vb:64)
A scratch space source starts as an empty policy store and is always writable. (PolicyPlus/PolicyLoader.vb:80)
When the POL file does not exist, the program creates its folder and an empty POL file and the source is writable; every setting starts Not configured. (PolicyPlus/PolicyLoader.vb:94)
When the missing POL file or its folder cannot be created, the source is an empty unsaved policy store and is not writable. (PolicyPlus/PolicyLoader.vb:101)
When a source has no comment file path, its comments are unavailable. (PolicyPlus/Main.vb:330)
